Notes: c. 41-42 CE (reign of Agrippa I; Claudius' edict of 41; Publius Petronius legate of Syria 39-42): Josephus, Antiquities 19.6.3 (19.300-311): young Greeks of Dora placed a statue of Claudius in the synagogue of the Jews; Agrippa I complained and Petronius ordered the magistrates of Dora to hand over the culprits, affirming the Jews' right to their customs and to equal civic standing (synpoliteuesthai). CIIP (Ameling et al.) concludes Dor 'at the time was a mixed town with city status and enough Jews to maintain a building for their synagogue' - an organized Jewish community with a synagogue; no count. CIIP adds: 'Thereafter there is no evidence for the presence of Jews in the town.' (Hostages held at Dora by Cestius Gallus in 66 CE were from Sepphoris - Josephus, Life 30-31 - not Dor residents.)
